# Limitations and unverified items

This document exists because the PRD requires unsupported input and unverified compatibility to be
disclosed rather than implied. Read it before using the output for design.

## 1. STAAD.Pro compatibility is unverified

* Files generated by this application **have not been executed in a licensed STAAD.Pro 2022 or 2025
  installation** as part of this build. The adapters for both releases are marked `unverified` in the
  header, the settings panel and the generated comment block.
* No verified grammatical difference between the 2022 and 2025 releases has been established for the
  commands used here, so none is simulated. The adapters exist so a demonstrated difference can be
  introduced in one place.
* The application's own parser round-trips the output; that proves internal consistency only. A file
  that looks syntactically plausible is not a passing test.

### Release gates that remain open

| Gate | Status |
|---|---|
| Run generated moving-load files in STAAD.Pro 2022 | **not run** |
| Run generated static-placement files in STAAD.Pro 2025 | **not run** |
| Confirm generated load positions/counts against the application preview | **not run** in STAAD |
| Confirm joint force directions under a non-default coordinate mapping | **not run** in STAAD |
| Independent hand-calculation comparison for a representative case | **not run** |
| Cross-version regression suite on real installations | **not run** |

Internal verification that *has* been done: 89 automated tests covering the engineering model, the
generators, the parser, reconstruction and the UI integration.

## 2. Supported command subset

Recognised and generated:

```
DEFINE MOVING LOAD   TYPE n LOAD … DISTANCE … [WIDTH …]
LOAD GENERATION n    TYPE t x y z XINC|YINC|ZINC increment
LOAD n LOADTYPE … TITLE …
JOINT LOAD           node [FX f] [FY f] [FZ f]
JOINT COORDINATES    / MEMBER INCIDENCES / ELEMENT INCIDENCES SHELL / UNIT …
```

Everything else is **preserved and reported**, not interpreted: `DEFINE LANE`, `VEHICLE`, load
combinations and load lists, member/plate/shell load items, unknown keywords, non-metric `UNIT`
statements. Those lines remain in the source text with a reason and line number.

Not implemented:

* member, plate, floor or surface load generation for vehicles;
* lane/floor moving-load references (`LANE …`, `FLOOR LOAD` moving vehicles);
* moving-load transverse ranges beyond the single sweep line, and multi-lane sweeps in one command;
* automatic critical-position search.

## 3. Moving-load representation limits

* A moving-load definition is a set of loads along **one longitudinal line**. The transverse position
  of a wheel pair is approximated by the line's transverse coordinate (explicit wheel lines) or by
  `WIDTH` (load-line idealisation). Arbitrary wheel coordinates cannot be expressed.
* When a vehicle's axle gauges differ, a single line cannot follow them; the app warns and uses the
  first axle's gauge.
* Tracked vehicles are discretised into equal slices; the discretisation (`trackSlices`) changes the
  load positions between the slice centres and must be chosen for the responses of interest.
* The sweep is linear with constant increments in one global axis. Rotated mappings are blocked rather
  than approximated.
* Two successive vehicles on the same line are not generated; each placed vehicle produces its own
  definition and type number.

## 4. Static-placement limits

* Load cases are produced **only** when a structural model is supplied. Without joints the app shows
  the intended placement and explicitly states that no structural load case was created.
* A wheel that falls outside every member/quad, or further than the joint tolerance from a joint,
  produces an error and a rejected case — never a silent snap. The nearest-joint method is the only
  method that snaps, and every snap distance is reported.
* Load transfer is per load point only. The app does not distribute loads along members as a
  consistent load at the model level, does not consider member eccentricity or local axes, and does
  not perform sub-meshing.
* Loads are vertical only (`FX = FZ = 0` in the default mapping). No braking, centrifugal or
  longitudinal forces are generated.
* Plate/shell models: the four-joint bilinear method is a load idealisation, not a substitute for a
  proper influence-surface analysis of a slab.
* Deck elevation is taken from the model joints; the app does not create or move joints.

## 5. Engineering scope

* No code-compliance checking, no load-factor combinations, no impact-factor derivation.
* No critical-position search, no influence lines, no envelope generation.
* No multi-lane live-load reduction, no successive-vehicle spacing rules, no footpath loading.
* Class A transverse gauge, Class 70R occupancy and kerb clearances are used for warnings only.
* Contact patches for the 70R wheeled/bogie definitions are nominal (see
  [vehicle-data.md](vehicle-data.md)).

## 6. Browser and environment

* Persistence uses `localStorage`; clearing site data removes the saved project. Use `Export JSON` for
  durable records.
* Clipboard access can be blocked in sandboxed frames; the copy buttons fall back to a hidden textarea
  and may still be refused by the browser.
* The canvas supports pointer, wheel and keyboard operations; it is usable on tablets, but the dense
  panels are designed for desktop widths.
